claim: Candidate donor mechanisms inform measured DiscoBSD/Pico compatibility work; this ledger makes no POSIX or UNIX conformance claim.
selection_rule: Prefer bounded algorithms, invariants, and tests. Admit code only after license, dependency, C17, ABI, RAM, linked-image, packed-root, and runtime gates agree.

candidates.behavior: Multiply element count by element size without wrapping; preserve the original allocation on failure and report an allocation error.
invariants: The product reaches realloc only when size_t can represent it.
A failed resize leaves the caller-owned allocation valid.
Zero-size behavior stays aligned with the target realloc contract.
candidates.algorithm: Guard multiplication before delegating to realloc; translate an overflow result to the target errno contract.
candidates.c_language: The function body is C17-compatible, but the donor uses NetBSD cdefs, namespace, and reallocarr interfaces.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Implement the overflow guard directly with C17 size_t arithmetic and the existing DiscoBSD allocator and errno interfaces.
candidates.deciding_gate: Re-run the behavior, archive-member, consumer-map, clean distribution, per-program and packed-root gates after changes to reallocarray or its consumers.
candidates.residual: The libc mechanism is promoted. The DPUCP requirement row stays open until an Issue 8 facet audit demonstrates that the executable witness covers the complete cited interface contract.

candidates.behavior: Locate the first bytewise needle in a bounded haystack, including the empty-needle and shorter-haystack cases.
invariants: The search reads only within the supplied haystack and needle extents.
An empty needle returns the haystack start.
The first matching position wins.
candidates.algorithm: Use specialized rolling windows for two- through four-byte needles and a Two-Way search with a bad-character shift table for longer needles.
candidates.c_language: The algorithm is C17-compatible but uses NetBSD cdefs and a 256-entry automatic shift table whose stack cost is target-sensitive.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Rewrite target namespace seams and compare the donor Two-Way implementation with a smaller linear search before selecting an algorithm.
candidates.deciding_gate: Re-run the behavior, strict-C17, archive-member, consumer-map, clean distribution, per-program and packed-root gates after changes to memmem or its consumers.
candidates.residual: The compact linear libc mechanism is promoted. Whole-program runtime stack peaks remain unmeasured. The DPUCP requirement row stays open until an Issue 8 facet audit demonstrates that the executable witness covers the complete cited interface contract.

candidates.behavior: Read through and retain a delimiter, grow or reuse a caller-owned buffer, append a NUL byte, and let getline delegate to the newline case.
invariants: Returned byte counts exclude the appended NUL and include a consumed delimiter.
Growth rejects size_t wrap and results beyond ssize_t range.
Allocation failure does not discard the caller's current buffer.
EOF before any byte returns minus one; EOF after bytes returns those bytes.
candidates.algorithm: Scan buffered stdio spans with memchr, grow geometrically under overflow checks, copy complete spans, and expose getline as a one-line getdelim wrapper.
candidates.c_language: The portable control flow is C17, while donor locking, FILE internals, power-of-two helpers, and namespace aliases are NetBSD-specific.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Retain one shared engine but bind it to DiscoBSD stdio internals and one-function-per-member archive composition.
candidates.deciding_gate: Re-run the line-reading behavior, sanitizer, strict-C17, archive-member, consumer-map, clean distribution, per-program and packed-root gates after changes to getdelim, getline or their consumers.
candidates.residual: The shared getdelim engine and thin getline wrapper are promoted. Whole-program runtime heap and stack peaks, including allocator metadata and unrelated callers, remain unmeasured. Their DPUCP requirement rows stay open until an Issue 8 facet audit demonstrates that the executable witness covers each complete cited interface contract.

roles: modern behavior oracle and repair reference
candidates.behavior: The 4.4BSD state machine supplies compact argument and character cursors, but it diagnoses both error classes unconditionally, reports question mark for both, and delays OPTIND publication until termination. The modern FreeBSD source supplies leading-colon results, per-call OPTIND and OPTARG updates, and explicit reset behavior.
invariants: Parser position consists of an argument index and an offset within a clustered option.
The double-dash operand ends option scanning.
Missing operands and illegal options select distinct silent and diagnostic results.
Reset behavior follows assignments to OPTIND rather than stale hidden state.
candidates.algorithm: Retain the historical next-argument and intra-argument cursors, then apply the modern error-result, variable-publication, explicit-argument and reset transitions after each call.
candidates.c_language: The 4.4BSD donor uses K&R definitions, register declarations, BSD __P prototypes, and shell-global state; the modern repair reference uses C17-compatible prototypes with FreeBSD shell allocators and interrupt guards.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Translate the state machine to strict C17 prototypes and explicit target shell state while preserving the first-release ILP32 boundary.
candidates.deciding_gate: Re-run the OPTIND, OPTARG, leading-colon, missing-operand, illegal-option, clustered-option, repeated-call, explicit-argument, reset, cross-build, linked-shell, process-window, and packed-root witnesses after changes to the getopts state machine.
candidates.residual: The C17 rewrite and measured compatibility subset are promoted. Runtime peak shell stack and heap remain unmeasured, and the positive shell and packed-root deltas require the recorded independent growth-exception approval before merge.

candidates.behavior: Report names with -v and -V through the shell's full reporting categories, while execution bypasses functions, removes special-builtin execution properties, and optionally selects the standards path with -p.
invariants: Reporting can identify aliases, keywords, functions, builtins and external paths without becoming the execution algorithm.
Execution through command sets the no-function lookup mode, so a shell function cannot shadow the selected command.
A special builtin invoked through command loses its special execution properties.
Lookup failure produces the specified nonzero status and diagnostic.
The -p path selection does not mutate the caller's PATH.
candidates.algorithm: Use exec.c reporting for terse and verbose descriptions, but use eval.c execution dispatch with no-function flags, special-property removal, command hashing, and an optional default utility path.
dependencies: evaluation dispatch and no-function lookup flag
candidates.c_language: The donor is modern C with FreeBSD cdefs and shell-private data structures that cannot be copied independently.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Port the precedence and status invariants into the existing DiscoBSD shell lookup machinery without importing FreeBSD hash-table dependencies.
candidates.deciding_gate: Re-run reporting-order, function-shadowing execution, special-builtin execution, -p, -v, -V, failure-status, diagnostic, cross-build, linked-shell, process-window, and packed-root witnesses after changes to command lookup or dispatch.
candidates.residual: The shared lookup and dispatch mechanisms and measured compatibility subset are promoted. Runtime peak shell stack and heap remain unmeasured, and the positive shell and packed-root deltas require the recorded independent growth-exception approval before merge.

candidates.behavior: Reuse the format until operands are exhausted, implement percent-b and backslash-c, bound dynamic width and precision, and return failure for malformed numeric input.
invariants: Backslash-c stops all remaining output immediately.
Percent-b interprets escapes in the operand without treating embedded NUL as a C-string terminator during emission.
A format is reused only when the previous pass consumed an operand.
Conversion diagnostics accumulate a nonzero final status.
candidates.algorithm: Parse one conversion at a time, normalize field width and precision, dispatch typed conversions, interpret escapes in place, and loop over the format while arguments advance.
candidates.c_language: The donor is modern C but depends on intmax, wide-character, locale, floating-point, err, and FreeBSD compatibility helpers.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Retain only the selected byte-locale behavior, target numeric conversions, and bounded parser states; exclude unselected locale tables and heavyweight helpers.

surfaces: standalone printf a.out text, data, bss, raw and packed bytes
utilbox a.out text, data, admitted bss, raw and packed bytes
standalone and utilbox libc archive-member maps

candidates.deciding_gate: Pass percent-b, backslash-c, embedded-NUL, repeated-format, width, precision, malformed-format, numeric-error, and final-status witnesses and preserve all constrained surfaces.
candidates.residual: The selected byte-locale subset is implemented and measured with a pending growth exception. Keep the Base requirement open until every required XBD File Format Notation facet and utility-specific exception has an executable witness and the approved complete-image measurement remains within its retained margins. Treat floating conversions and positional star operands as optional extensions, and mixed numbering as unspecified behavior.

candidates.behavior: Read one symbolic-link value without following it, write the exact path text, and control trailing newline behavior.
invariants: The output buffer reserves one byte for an explicit terminator.
A readlink failure reaches the utility exit status.
The applet emits link bytes exactly once and adds only the selected newline.
candidates.algorithm: Validate one operand, call readlink into a bounded buffer, terminate the returned byte span, and emit it through binary-safe output primitives.
dependencies: PATH_MAX policy or bounded dynamic buffer
candidates.c_language: The donor body is C17-compatible but uses OpenBSD pledge, err, getopt globals, and host PATH_MAX assumptions.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Use existing DiscoBSD syscall, diagnostics, and textbox dispatch while selecting a buffer strategy from target path limits and stack measurements.

surfaces: standalone readlink a.out text, data, bss, raw and packed bytes
textbox a.out text, data, bss, raw and packed bytes
standalone and textbox libc archive-member maps

candidates.deciding_gate: Pass symlink, empty target where supported, maximum target, non-link, missing path, newline, and write-error witnesses and compare standalone against textbox packed-root composition.
candidates.residual: The one-operand and newline-control subset is implemented and measured through the shared textbox image. Keep the Base requirement partial and open until the remaining Issue 8 facets have executable witnesses and target execution confirms the selected behavior. Runtime peak stack and heap remain unmeasured.

candidates.behavior: Canonicalize one path with the existing libc resolver, select whether the final component must exist through -e or -E, and write one canonical path line.
invariants: Path resolution remains owned by libc rather than duplicated in the applet.
A successful operand emits one canonical path line.
A resolution or output failure reaches the utility exit status.
candidates.algorithm: Validate one operand, resolve a bounded chain of final symbolic links, delegate canonicalization to libc realpath, optionally admit one missing final component, and emit the resulting path.
dependencies: PATH_MAX policy or bounded dynamic buffer
candidates.c_language: The donor body is C17-compatible but uses FreeBSD cdefs, err, and PATH_MAX interfaces.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Keep only the thin applet wrapper and bind it to the existing DiscoBSD realpath and textbox facilities.

surfaces: standalone realpath a.out text, data, bss, raw and packed bytes
textbox a.out text, data, bss, raw and packed bytes
standalone and textbox libc archive-member maps

candidates.deciding_gate: Pass one-operand, relative, dot-dot, symlink, missing-final, missing-prefix, trailing-slash, write-error, and option-precedence witnesses and prove textbox composition is smaller than a standalone utility.
candidates.residual: The one-operand -e and -E subset is implemented and measured through the shared textbox image. Keep the Base requirement partial and open until the remaining Issue 8 facets have executable witnesses and target execution confirms the selected behavior. Runtime peak stack and heap remain unmeasured beyond the bounded 672-byte static frame.

candidates.behavior: Run a command under a duration, deliver the selected signal on expiry, forward relevant signals, and map timeout, execution, exit, and signal results accurately.
invariants: Only a verified timer expiry selects timeout status 124 unless preserve-status applies.
Signal forwarding reaches the child execution group supported by the target kernel.
Exec-not-found and exec-not-invokable remain distinguishable as 127 and 126.
The wrapper reproduces a child's signal termination when the target primitives permit it.
candidates.algorithm: Install signal handlers, arm a real-time interval, spawn and monitor the child, forward or escalate signals, and derive final status from wait results.
candidates.c_language: The FreeBSD donor is modern C but depends on procctl reapers, siginfo, wait6, resource limits, getopt_long and floating-duration helpers. NetBSD retains the older FreeBSD-derived signal-flag state machine. OpenBSD adds pledge and strtonum while retaining the same waitpid, process-group and interval-timer core.
candidates.c17_rewrite: The target-native strict-C17 state machine uses the verified interval-timer, waitpid, signal and process-group primitives. It omits reaper, pledge, long-option and floating-duration machinery outside the selected subset.

surfaces: adminbox a.out text, data, bss, raw and packed bytes
standalone timeout a.out text, data, bss, raw and packed bytes
PICO and PICO_UART kernel region occupancy
packed Dhara root blocks and free-block margin

candidates.deciding_gate: Pass native alarm, kill, waitpid, process-group forwarding, signal escalation, stop-and-continue, execution-status, timeout-status and preserve-status witnesses; compile the exact source under strict C17 for Cortex-M0+; link the target a.out; and admit the measured adminbox and packed-root growth exception.
candidates.residual: The selected -f, -k, -p and -s subset is implemented in adminbox and measured through host, strict-C17 cross, target-link and packed-root gates. Keep the utility requirement partial and open until target execution confirms timer, wait-status, process-group and signal-delivery behavior. Renode and physical-board execution remain unrun, and whole-program runtime stack and heap peaks remain unmeasured.

candidates.behavior: The donor decodes traditional uuencoded and optional base64 input and supports an output override, but its traditional loop trusts encoded line length and both decoding paths ignore output-call results. The target must add binary-clean -o - output, payload validation, and write-error propagation.
invariants: The target repair keeps decoded stdout byte-clean and sends diagnostics elsewhere.
The target repair validates header, encoded line length and payload characters before indexed access.
The target repair maps output-open, put and write failures to nonzero status.
The stdout destination bypasses file permissions and path expansion.
candidates.algorithm: Use the donor's begin-header and four-character to three-byte decoding structure, but bound every group by the available encoded line and route all decoded bytes through one checked target output sink.
dependencies: file creation only for non-stdout destinations
candidates.c_language: The donor is modern C but depends on NetBSD cdefs, err, passwd lookup, resolver base64 support, mode handling, tilde expansion, and file-output policy beyond the selected stdout path.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Refactor a strict-C17 decoder core around the existing applet, preserve current file behavior, and add one output-sink abstraction for -o - without heap-backed registries.

surfaces: uudecode a.out text, data, bss, raw and packed bytes

candidates.deciding_gate: Pass binary-NUL stdout, malformed-header, malformed traditional line, missing traditional footer, write-failure, file-output regression, and packed-root witnesses.
candidates.residual: The binary-clean -o - and checked-output subset is implemented and measured. Keep the Base requirement partial and open until the remaining Issue 8 facets have executable witnesses. Complete base64 padding and ==== footer validation remains open because incomplete base64 input can return success after emitting decoded bytes. Runtime peak stack and heap remain unmeasured.

candidates.behavior: Number selected logical-page lines, including pBRE selection, without giving nl a private regular-expression implementation.
invariants: Header, body, and footer selectors share one numbering state machine.
A pBRE selector uses the same byte-locale BRE semantics as other selected utilities.
Private regex code cannot enter nl merely to close one requirement row.
candidates.algorithm: Parse section selectors and formatting controls, detect logical-page delimiters, and apply a shared compiled BRE only for pattern-selected numbering.
candidates.c_language: The donor is modern C but pulls regex, locale, multibyte, wide-character, Capsicum, and host utility support that exceed the first-release boundary.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Retain the numbering state machine and byte-locale behavior only after a shared strict-C17 BRE provider is admitted for all consumers.
candidates.deciding_gate: Admit a shared compact BRE provider first, then pass selector, logical-page, formatting, invalid-BRE, byte-locale, link-map, and packed-root witnesses.
candidates.residual: The target lacks a shared compact BRE provider; keep pBRE open until the later BRE/ERE family closes that prerequisite.

candidates.behavior: Partition comparator-equal records together and carry typed comparator context per call.
invariants: Equal-key blocks leave the recursive partitions.
The target recurses only into the smaller partition, bounding stack depth by log2(element count).
Nested comparator calls preserve independent contexts; callback casts cannot substitute for compatible types.
candidates.algorithm: Bentley-McIlroy three-way partitioning and sampled pivots. Compose equal-key grouping with local smaller-side recursion; evaluate an introspective depth budget and allocation-free byte-swap heap fallback for worst-case comparison bounds.
dependencies: existing local qsort and allocating heapsort implementations
candidates.c_language: Donor C and private BSD interfaces require target GNU17 compilation, strict C17 mechanism checks and separate Smaller C declaration acceptance.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Use typed context-last callbacks for Issue 8. The donor uses context-first callbacks and always recurses left, so neither its public signature nor its recursion policy transfers unchanged.
candidates.deciding_gate: Compare exhaustive small arrays and large equal-heavy, sorted, reverse, periodic and comparator-adversarial inputs against an independent order/permutation oracle; test nested contexts, count comparisons and measure target stack/text and clean consumer artifacts.
candidates.residual: The algorithms have prior art. Port-specific composition remains unimplemented and resource-unmeasured; the existing allocating heapsort cannot silently supply a non-failing fallback.

candidates.behavior: Expose fixed-capacity storage through stdio with explicit cursor, logical extent and termination rules.
invariants: The cursor and every backing-buffer access remain inside the admitted extent.
Capacity, logical extent and terminating-byte placement remain distinct.
Append selects its contractually defined write position after seek.
candidates.algorithm: Backend cookie tracks fixed storage; translate callbacks through a private target FILE backend and its existing buffering/lifetime rules.
candidates.c_language: Donor C and private BSD interfaces require target GNU17 compilation, strict C17 mechanism checks and separate Smaller C declaration acceptance.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Rederive read and write bounds from the standard. The donor read callback uses the remaining capacity rather than the logical extent; donor output alone is not an independent oracle.
candidates.deciding_gate: Exercise all modes, embedded NULs, zero/full capacities, exact-full writes, append-after-seek, flush/close termination, allocation failure and cleanup against explicit normative cases.
candidates.residual: Private backend design and shared-libc state ownership precede implementation; host behavior does not establish target memory use.

candidates.behavior: Publish caller-owned pointer and length at the required stdio synchronization boundaries.
invariants: Capacity, logical extent, cursor and published pointer/length are separate state.
Growth failure preserves the owned allocation and a coherent stream.
Every admitted growth accounts for the old-plus-new moving-realloc peak and a terminating byte.
candidates.algorithm: Adapt the cookie mechanism with checked geometric capacity growth for amortized linear copying; the donor exact-size allocation can copy quadratically during repeated small writes.
candidates.c_language: Donor C and private BSD interfaces require target GNU17 compilation, strict C17 mechanism checks and separate Smaller C declaration acceptance.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Keep stream position and logical end independent of allocated capacity and publication; use overflow-checked conversions before growth or seeking.
candidates.deciding_gate: Test backward overwrite, seek holes, embedded NULs, maximal offsets, failed growth, flush/close publication and cleanup; count copied bytes over append sequences and measure target peak allocations.
candidates.residual: The growth strategy is established prior art. Publication details and target resource admission remain open; allocation savings do not replace peak-memory evidence.

candidates.behavior: Establish the C/POSIX byte locale and restartable conversion state before a later UTF-8 profile.
invariants: Byte conversion handles NUL, reset and zero available bytes explicitly.
A selected encoding defines high-byte acceptance and invalid wide values.
A later UTF-8 state tracks partial scalar, remaining continuation bytes and the shortest-form lower bound.
candidates.algorithm: Stateless unsigned-byte mapping is the initial candidate. Retain the UTF-8 state-machine comparison separately; validate Unicode scalar exclusions as well as shortest forms.
dependencies: restartable conversion pointer and errno rules
candidates.c_language: Donor C and private BSD interfaces require target GNU17 compilation, strict C17 mechanism checks and separate Smaller C declaration acceptance.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Implement the selected byte contract first. A later UTF-8 parser explicitly rejects surrogate scalars and values above U+10FFFF; the donor range predicate alone admits surrogates.
candidates.deciding_gate: Exercise every byte, NUL/reset/incomplete states, null state/output, invalid wide values and source-pointer publication. A later UTF-8 gate exercises every split and malformed sequence class.
candidates.residual: UTF-8 remains outside the initial byte-locale contract. Neither source file establishes target type layout, concurrency semantics or runtime resource cost.

candidates.behavior: Parse calendar fields with explicit presence flags and derive only the fields supported by the parsed inputs.
invariants: Unspecified fields retain their required state.
Century and year composition follows field-presence rules.
Parsing reports the correct trailing input and rejects invalid directives or values.
candidates.algorithm: Presence flags separate primary parsed fields from derived calendar fields; reconcile century, leap-year and week calculations after parsing.
candidates.c_language: Donor C and private BSD interfaces require target GNU17 compilation, strict C17 mechanism checks and separate Smaller C declaration acceptance.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Rederive directive ranges, omitted-field rules and composite recursion. The donor rejects centuries below 19, so its accepted domain cannot define the target contract.
candidates.deciding_gate: Test omitted fields, centuries below and above 19, leap dates, week/year boundaries, composite directives, trailing percent, trailing input and overflow with independent calendar oracles.
candidates.residual: Calendar parsing stays separate from kernel clocks, monotonic time and interrupted sleep.

candidates.behavior: Apply ordered descriptor and process-state actions before executable admission and communicate launch errors with explicit ownership.
invariants: File actions replay in insertion order.
Parent and child retain defined ownership of action storage, stack and failure communication.
Exec failure and interrupted waits preserve cleanup and child-reaping contracts.
candidates.algorithm: Ordered action list and staged attributes provide reusable structure. The donor vfork/shared-stack error channel needs a separate proof for the flat process window.
candidates.c_language: Donor C and private BSD interfaces require target GNU17 compilation, strict C17 mechanism checks and separate Smaller C declaration acceptance.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Use native error-number returns and typed action records. Investigate donor allocation-failure return -1 against the POSIX error-number contract; avoid importing the donor error convention.
candidates.deciding_gate: Test descriptor collisions, CLOEXEC, ordered open/close/dup, signal defaults/masks, action and exec failures, allocation exhaustion, parent stack integrity and child reaping in the target process model.
candidates.residual: Donor source supplies a mechanism candidate, not a proof that local vfork or spawn is implementable with the same ownership. Kernel prerequisites remain visible.

candidates.behavior: Reject a basename before allocation or I/O unless both four-byte suffixes and the terminator fit the 1,024-byte buffer; acquire two files transactionally; admit the directory extent before publishing its maximum bit index.
invariants: A basename length above 1,019 returns ENAMETOOLONG without allocation or file operations.
Each failure releases exactly the allocation and descriptors already acquired and preserves the failing stage's errno.
An empty directory publishes -1; positive extent n publishes 8 * (n - 1) + 7 only when the result fits long.
The public constructor type is DBM *dbm_open(const char *, int, mode_t).
candidates.algorithm: Use one bounded scan, direct suffix copies, descriptor sentinels and an overflow-free positive-extent form. The composition retains the local two-file representation and avoids formatter linkage.
candidates.c_language: The public header and constructor seam use complete C17-compatible prototypes; the remainder of ndbm.c retains old-style definitions under a separate migration-open row.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Retain the historical storage representation and notices; type the exported boundary, close the two maintained two-argument callers and make admission arithmetic explicit.

surfaces: shipped program text/data/BSS and packed bytes
maximum constructor stack and allocation extent

candidates.deciding_gate: Run the aggregate host, cross, QEMU and ILP32 gates on the merged candidate; retain the matched clean static-resource verdict; review before promotion.
candidates.residual: Focused native, ILP32 and ARMv6-M constructor witnesses and matched shipped static-resource qualification pass. Aggregate gates, reviewed integration, runtime resources, remaining ndbm semantics and physical-board behavior remain open.

candidates.behavior: Bound scans and duplication by the supplied extent; return the copied terminator or the end of the bounded destination; pad stpncpy through exactly n bytes.
invariants: strnlen reads at most maxlen bytes and stops at the first NUL.
strndup admits length plus one before allocation and terminates the successful result.
stpcpy returns the copied NUL address; stpncpy returns the first written NUL or destination plus n.
All state is per call; nonallocating operations preserve errno.
candidates.algorithm: Use bytewise loops and one bounded-length allocation. Distinguish the first terminator position from the padding cursor.
candidates.c_language: The definitions use strict C17 prototypes and restrict; public declarations remain accepted by Smaller C.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Preserve the donor notices and bytewise loops; replace private restrict spelling and reject SIZE_MAX before adding the terminator byte.
candidates.deciding_gate: Run check-libc-bounded-string, check-string-header-contracts, native archive linkage, Thumb-1 execution, matched clean distributions and resource comparison before promotion.
candidates.residual: The implementation and calibrated behavior fixtures exist. Matched static captures measure 692 additional native archive bytes with all other measured surfaces unchanged; docs/research/libc-bounded-string-resource-exception.md binds the receipts and pending review. Runtime resource qualification, aggregate gates and integration remain open; the unmeasured size state retains that incomplete qualification.

candidates.behavior: Return the representable mathematical magnitude through public callable int and long providers.
invariants: The input type determines the result type.
Unrepresentable mathematical magnitudes remain outside the defined contract.
Each provider has its own archive member and imports no runtime symbol.
candidates.algorithm: Typed conditional negation uses constant work and constant automatic storage.
dependencies: cross and native archive member selection
candidates.c_language: GNU17 production and strict C17 probes; Smaller C consumes public address-taking declarations.
candidates.c17_rewrite: Independent typed definitions follow C17 7.22.6.1. Coherent and DragonFlyBSD comparisons corroborate the representability boundary; no bit-pattern or signed-shift assumption enters the source.
candidates.deciding_gate: Run check-libc-absolute-value, check-c17-headers-cross, full/reduced native archive omission controls, Smaller C and matched clean resource captures.
candidates.residual: Cross objects each occupy eight text bytes with no imports, data or BSS. Whole-image resource admission and aggregate qualification remain open. docs/research/libc-absolute-value-contracts.md records source identities, defined-domain witnesses and limitations.
